# webhooks.cc full reference

> Webhook and email testing tools for developers. Capture, inspect, forward, and test webhooks and email with a dashboard, CLI, SDKs for TypeScript, Python and Go, and an MCP server for AI agents.

## What is webhooks.cc?

webhooks.cc is a webhook inspection and testing service. Developers use it to capture incoming HTTP requests at unique URLs, inspect headers and bodies in real time, configure mock responses with conditional rules (route different responses based on method, path, headers, body, or query params), forward webhooks to localhost for local development, and write automated test assertions against captured requests.

Every endpoint on an account also receives email at `<slug>@mailhooks.cc` (Business adds custom inbound domains). Captured emails sit in the same request list as webhooks; layouts can read fields, line items and CSV, Excel or PDF attachments out of them, and destinations send them (and HTTP requests) on to your servers, Slack or Discord, Google Sheets, or SFTP, FTP and S3 file drops. mailhooks.cc is the mail-first front door to the same accounts, endpoints and plans.

The Rust receiver handles 86,000+ requests per second with sub-millisecond capture latency. Requests are written directly to Postgres via a single stored procedure and surfaced in the dashboard through Supabase Realtime.

## Architecture

- **Dashboard**: Next.js App Router with real-time updates via Supabase Realtime Broadcast signals (database triggers send id-only signals on private topics; the dashboard then re-reads through authenticated API routes)
- **Receiver**: Rust (Axum + Tokio) writing directly to Postgres via sqlx and a single stored procedure
- **Email intake**: a receive-only Rust SMTP host for `mailhooks.cc` that hands each message to the receiver, which stores it through the same stored procedure as webhooks
- **Forwarding**: a queue drained by the web app, which delivers each capture to the endpoint's destinations (up to 10), each with its own filter, format and retries
- **Database**: Self-hosted Supabase (Postgres) with row-level security
- **CLI**: Rust (Clap + Ratatui) connecting via SSE streams
- **SDKs**: TypeScript (`@webhooks-cc/sdk` on npm), Python (`webhooks-cc` on PyPI) and Go (`webhooks.cc/go`); the Python and Go SDKs pass the TypeScript SDK's conformance vectors
- **MCP Server**: a remote server at https://webhooks.cc/mcp (streamable HTTP, OAuth) and the same tools as a local TypeScript server (`@webhooks-cc/mcp`) for AI coding agents

## URLs

- Homepage: https://webhooks.cc
- Webhook receiver: https://go.webhooks.cc
- Endpoint URL format: `https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>` or `https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>/optional/path`
- Endpoint email address format: `<slug>@mailhooks.cc` or `<slug>+<tag>@mailhooks.cc`
- Documentation: https://webhooks.cc/docs
- Email capture: https://webhooks.cc/docs/email-capture
- Email forwarding: https://webhooks.cc/docs/forwarding
- REST API: https://webhooks.cc/docs/api
- OpenAPI spec: https://webhooks.cc/openapi.yaml
- Installation: https://webhooks.cc/installation
- Remote MCP server: https://webhooks.cc/mcp (setup at https://webhooks.cc/docs/mcp#remote-server)
- AI agents: https://webhooks.cc/docs/agents and https://webhooks.cc/auth.md
- GitHub: https://github.com/kroqdotdev/webhooks-cc
- npm SDK: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@webhooks-cc/sdk
- npm MCP: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@webhooks-cc/mcp

## Pricing

- **Guest** (no signup): 25 requests per ephemeral endpoint, deleted after 12 hours, no email capture
- **Free**: 50 requests per 24 hours, unlimited endpoints, 7-day retention, 20 parsed attachment pages a month, 2 layouts per endpoint, 5 AI assists every 30 days, every Pro feature including email capture, Google Sheets and chat destinations and full CLI/SDK/MCP access
- **Pro** ($8/month): 100,000 requests a month, 31-day retention, 100 parsed attachment pages a month, 20 AI assists every 30 days. Extra requests: monthly blocks ($2 per 25,000), one-time blocks ($3 per 25,000) or overage ($4 per 25,000, up to a maximum you set).
- **Business** ($29/month, or $290/year; annual billing is only for Business and Team Business): 250,000 requests a month, 90-day retention, 2,000 parsed attachment pages a month, up to 50 layouts per endpoint, 250 AI assists every 30 days, one custom inbound domain (each extra one $3/month, up to 20 domains in all), file drops to SFTP, FTP/FTPS or S3-compatible storage, extra requests as on Pro. More pages: monthly page blocks ($5 per 1,000), one-time page blocks ($8 per 1,000, never expire) or opt-in page overage ($0.01 per page, up to a maximum you set). On annual billing requests and pages still reset every month.
- **Teams** ($12/seat/month, from 2 seats, monthly only): a separate per-team subscription, not a tier of a personal plan. Each seat adds 100,000 requests a month to a pooled team quota and one member slot. Requests on endpoints shared with an active team are billed to the pool and kept 31 days.
- **Team Business** ($35/seat/month or $350/seat/year, from 2 seats): the team's plan with Business per seat: 250,000 requests, 2,000 parsed attachment pages (with page blocks and overage) and 250 AI assists per seat, pooled for the team, up to 50 layouts per endpoint on team-shared endpoints, one custom inbound domain per team, file drops for team-shared endpoints, and 90-day retention for team-billed requests. On annual billing the allowance still renews every month. Moving up from Teams applies at once, charged and granted for the rest of the period in proportion; moving down waits for the renewal. Members' personal endpoints follow their own plan.
- A parsed page is each PDF page (text layer, no OCR), each started 1,000 rows of each sheet in CSV/TSV/XLSX/XLS/ODS, or each plain text attachment; email bodies never count. Without pages left, emails still arrive with attachments as files, unparsed.
- Emails count against the same quota as webhooks: one request per email per endpoint it is addressed to.

## Authentication

API keys use the `whcc_` prefix. Generate from https://webhooks.cc/account or via `whk auth login`.

Protected endpoints require a Bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer whcc_...
```

AI agents have two more ways in, and both end in the same kind of token:

- **OAuth, for remote MCP clients.** The remote MCP server at https://webhooks.cc/mcp sends its client through OAuth 2.1 (authorization code with PKCE; Client ID Metadata Documents or dynamic client registration). The human signs in and clicks Connect once; there is no key to paste or code to type. See https://webhooks.cc/docs/agents#apps-connected-with-oauth.
- **Agent registration (auth.md).** An agent without an account registers itself, gets a 24-hour sandbox, and a human can claim it into their account with a link and a 6-digit code. See https://webhooks.cc/auth.md and https://webhooks.cc/docs/agents.

The access tokens agents get either way are short-lived `whcc_` tokens, sent in the same `Authorization: Bearer` header as an API key, so every route accepts them unchanged. Connected agents and OAuth apps never reach API keys, billing or account settings, and are listed (and disconnected) under Account, Connected agents.

Public routes (no API key, session or access token; most are rate limited per IP):

- CLI device flow: `POST /api/auth/device-code`, `GET /api/auth/device-poll`, `POST /api/auth/device-claim`
- Guest endpoints: `POST /api/go/endpoint`, `GET /api/go/endpoint/{slug}`, `GET /api/go/endpoint/{slug}/requests`
- Agent registration (auth.md): `POST /api/agent/identity/challenge`, `POST /api/agent/identity`, `POST /api/agent/identity/claim` (takes the `claim_token` in the body), `POST /api/agent/event/notify` (takes a signed Security Event Token from a trusted identity provider)
- OAuth: `POST /api/oauth2/token`, `POST /api/oauth2/register`, `POST /api/oauth2/revoke` (public clients, no client secret)

---

## TypeScript SDK Reference

Package: `@webhooks-cc/sdk` on npm.

### Installation

```bash
npm install @webhooks-cc/sdk
```

### Client Constructor

```typescript
import { WebhooksCC } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

const client = new WebhooksCC({
  apiKey: "whcc_...",         // Required
  baseUrl: "https://webhooks.cc",         // Optional
  webhookUrl: "https://go.webhooks.cc",   // Optional
  timeout: 30000,             // Request timeout in ms
  retry: {                    // Optional retry policy
    maxAttempts: 3,
    backoffMs: 1000,
    retryOn: [502, 503, 504],
  },
  hooks: {                    // Optional lifecycle hooks
    onRequest: (info) => {},
    onResponse: (info) => {},
    onError: (info) => {},
  },
  emailDomain: "mailhooks.cc", // Optional, the domain emails.address() uses
});
```

### Endpoints

```typescript
// Create endpoint
const endpoint = await client.endpoints.create({
  name?: string,              // Display name
  ephemeral?: boolean,        // Auto-expire
  expiresIn?: number | string,  // e.g. "12h"
  mockResponse?: MockResponse,
  responseRules?: ResponseRule[],  // Conditional response rules (first match wins)
  notificationUrl?: string,   // Slack/Discord URL
});
// Returns: Endpoint { id, slug, name, url, createdAt, ... }

// List all endpoints
const endpoints = await client.endpoints.list();
// Returns: Endpoint[]

// Get single endpoint
const ep = await client.endpoints.get("my-slug");

// Update endpoint
const updated = await client.endpoints.update("my-slug", {
  name?: string,
  mockResponse?: MockResponse | null,  // null clears mock
  responseRules?: ResponseRule[] | null,  // null clears all rules
  notificationUrl?: string | null,     // null clears notification
});

// Delete endpoint
await client.endpoints.delete("my-slug");

// Mark or unmark one of your favourites (yours, shared endpoints too);
// list() and get() carry favorite: boolean
await client.endpoints.favorite("my-slug");   // { favorite: true }
await client.endpoints.unfavorite("my-slug"); // { favorite: false }

// Send test webhook to your own endpoint
const response = await client.endpoints.send("my-slug", {
  method?: string,            // Default: "POST"
  headers?: Record<string, string>,
  body?: unknown,             // JSON-serialized if object
});

// Send provider webhook template
await client.endpoints.sendTemplate("my-slug", {
  provider: "stripe",        // stripe|github|shopify|twilio|slack|paddle|linear|sendgrid|clerk|discord|vercel|gitlab|typeform|standard-webhooks|meta|lemonsqueezy|coinbase-commerce|razorpay|cal|intercom|telegram|square|hubspot|mailgun|calendly|mux|sentry|bitbucket|docusign|adyen|paypal|plaid|resend|workos
  template?: string,         // Provider-specific preset
  secret: "whsec_test",      // Template signing input (omit for unsigned templates: sendgrid|discord|plaid)
  event?: string,            // Event type override
  timestamp?: number,        // For deterministic signatures
});
```

### Requests

```typescript
// List recent requests
const requests = await client.requests.list("my-slug", {
  limit?: number,
  since?: number,           // Timestamp in ms
  kind?: "http" | "email",  // Only HTTP requests or only emails
});

// Paginated listing
const page = await client.requests.listPaginated("my-slug", {
  limit?: number,
  cursor?: string,          // From previous page
  kind?: "http" | "email",
});
// Returns: { items: Request[], cursor?: string, hasMore: boolean }

// Get single request (emails have kind: "email" and the parsed message in `email`)
const req = await client.requests.get("request-id");

// Wait for next request (polling)
const req = await client.requests.waitFor("my-slug", {
  timeout?: number | string,     // Default: "30s", e.g. "5m"
  pollInterval?: number | string, // Default: "500ms"
  match?: (request: Request) => boolean,
  since?: number,                 // Default: five minutes ago, so a request that just arrived is found
});

// Wait for multiple requests
const reqs = await client.requests.waitForAll("my-slug", {
  count: 3,
  timeout?: number | string,
  match?: (request: Request) => boolean,
});

// Stream requests in real time (SSE)
for await (const req of client.requests.subscribe("my-slug", {
  signal?: AbortSignal,
  timeout?: number | string,
  reconnect?: boolean,
  maxReconnectAttempts?: number,  // Default: 5
})) {
  console.log(req.kind, req.method, req.path);  // streamed requests carry kind, not the parsed email
}

// Replay captured request to a URL (throws for emails)
const response = await client.requests.replay("request-id", "http://localhost:8080");

// Search requests
const results = await client.requests.search({
  slug?: string,
  method?: string,
  kind?: "http" | "email",
  q?: string,               // Free-text search
  from?: number | string,   // Start time
  to?: number | string,     // End time
  limit?: number,           // Default: 50
  offset?: number,
  order?: "asc" | "desc",
});

// Count matching requests
const count = await client.requests.count({ slug: "my-slug", method: "POST" });

// Clear requests
await client.requests.clear("my-slug", { before?: number | string });

// Export requests (HTTP only; emails are skipped)
const exported = await client.requests.export("my-slug", {
  format: "har" | "curl",
  limit?: number,
  since?: number,
});
```

### Emails

Every endpoint on an account receives email at `<slug>@mailhooks.cc` and `<slug>+<tag>@mailhooks.cc`; guest endpoints receive none. A captured email is a request with `kind: "email"`, `method: "EMAIL"`, the recipient address as `path`, the raw message as `body` and the parsed message as `email` (typed `EmailRequest`). An email counts as one request.

```typescript
import { extractCode, extractLink, extractFromEmail } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

// The address, optionally with a +tag (pass the Endpoint object to use its emailAddress)
const address = client.emails.address("my-slug", "run-42"); // "my-slug+run-42@mailhooks.cc"

// Criteria shared by list, latest, waitFor, waitForAll (all given criteria must match):
//   tag?: string | null        exact, case-sensitive; null = untagged mail only
//   subject?: string | RegExp  string = substring
//   from?: string | RegExp     string = address, case-insensitive; RegExp tested against "Name <address>"
//   to?: string | RegExp       To, Cc, or the address it was delivered to; same rules as from

// List emails, newest first (limit = newest emails fetched before filtering, default 50)
const emails = await client.emails.list("my-slug", { tag: "run-42", limit: 50, since: Date.now() - 60_000 });

// One email by request ID (NotFoundError if the request is not an email)
const one = await client.emails.get("request-id");

// The newest matching email among the 100 newest, or null
const latest = await client.emails.latest("my-slug", { subject: "Confirm" });

// Poll until a matching email arrives; throws TimeoutError
const email = await client.emails.waitFor("my-slug", {
  tag: "run-42",
  timeout: "60s",            // Default: 60000
  pollInterval: "1s",        // Default: 1000
  since: Date.now(),         // Default: five minutes ago
  match: (e) => e.email.attachments.length === 0,  // Extra filter
});

// Poll until `count` matching emails arrive, oldest first
const several = await client.emails.waitForAll("my-slug", { count: 2, tag: "run-42" });

// Deliver a sample email with a 6-digit code and a link (counts as one request, no SMTP, no sender checks)
const sent = await client.emails.sendTest("my-slug", { tag: "run-42" });
// Returns: { status: "captured", requestId: string | null }

// The email.received JSON forwarding would post (no API call)
const event = client.emails.toJson(email, {
  endpoint: { slug: "my-slug", name: "Signup flow" },  // Optional; fills data.endpoint.name
  includeExtracts: true,                                // Default: true (codes and links)
});

// Code and link finder (no API call); accepts a request or the parsed email
extractCode(email);                          // "482913" or null
extractLink(email);                          // action link (confirm, verify, reset, sign in), else the first link worth keeping
extractLink(email, { actionOnly: true });    // only an action link, or null
extractFromEmail(email.email);               // { codes: string[], links: { url, label, action }[] }
```

`@webhooks-cc/sdk/email` exports the email types (`EmailCapture`, `EmailReceivedEvent`, ...), `extractCode`, `extractLink`, `extractFromEmail`, `htmlToText`, `buildEmailJson`, `emailAddress` and `isValidEmailTag`, with no network code (browser-safe).

`requests.replay()` throws for emails, `requests.export()` skips them, and provider detection ignores them. Requests from `requests.subscribe()` carry `kind` but not `email`; call `client.emails.get(id)` for the parsed message.

### Destinations

An endpoint sends what it captures to up to 10 destinations, each with its own kinds (`http`, `email`), filter, format (`as_received`, `json`, `template`, `chat`, `sheets`, `file_drop`, or a mail provider's shape: `postmark`, `sendgrid`, `mailgun`, `cloudmailin`), throttle, delay and `whsec_` secret. Owner only.

```typescript
const dest = await client.destinations.create("my-slug", {
  url: "https://example.com/hooks",
  http: true,
  email: true,
  format: "json",
});
await client.destinations.list("my-slug", { summary: true }); // with the last 24 hours
await client.destinations.update("my-slug", dest.id, { throttleSeconds: 1 });
await client.destinations.secret("my-slug", dest.id);       // "whsec_..."
await client.destinations.test("my-slug", dest.id);         // one delivery now
await client.destinations.preview("my-slug", { destinationId: dest.id }); // dry run, nothing sent
await client.destinations.delete("my-slug", dest.id);
```

### Forwarding

`client.forwarding` manages the endpoint's primary destination (the one its `forwardUrl` and `forwardEnabled` fields stand for), so code written before destinations keeps working. Owner only: for anyone else these throw `NotFoundError` (`configure` fails with 403 for team members).

```typescript
// Set the URL and/or turn forwarding on or off; returns the Endpoint.
// The first URL creates the signing secret. url: null removes it (forwarding must be off).
await client.forwarding.configure("my-slug", { url: "https://example.com/hooks/email", enabled: true });

// The whsec_ signing secret (NotFoundError before a URL was saved)
const secret = await client.forwarding.secret("my-slug");

// Replace the secret; every delivery from now on, retries included, uses the new one
const rotated = await client.forwarding.rotateSecret("my-slug");

// Post the newest email (or a sample) to the URL once; works with forwarding on or off
const result = await client.forwarding.test("my-slug");
// Returns: { status: number | null, durationMs, excerpt: string | null, error: string | null, delivered: boolean, sample: boolean }

// The endpoint's latest deliveries, newest first (limit 1-20, default 5)
const recent = await client.forwarding.deliveries("my-slug", { limit: 10 });
// Returns: RecentEmailDelivery[] { id, requestId, status, attempts, createdAt, lastStatus, lastError, subject }

// Every delivery of one email, with each try in attemptLog
const deliveries = await client.forwarding.emailDeliveries("request-id");
// Returns: EmailDelivery[] (see Delivery under Forwarding below)

// Queue the email again with the current URL and secret (409 when forwarding is off)
const { id } = await client.forwarding.redeliver("request-id");
```

Verify a forwarded email in your handler. `verifyForwardedEmail` checks `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` (within `toleranceSeconds`, default 300) and `webhook-signature` against the raw body and the `whsec_` secret, then parses the body as an `email.received` event:

```typescript
import { verifyForwardedEmail, WebhookVerificationError } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  try {
    const event = await verifyForwardedEmail(
      await request.text(),       // raw body: string, Uint8Array (Buffer) or ArrayBuffer
      request.headers,            // Fetch Headers, a plain object (Node/Express req.headers) or [name, value] pairs
      process.env.FORWARD_SECRET!,
      { toleranceSeconds: 300 }   // Optional; also `now` (ms) for tests
    );
    console.log(event.data.subject, event.data.codes);
    return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof WebhookVerificationError) {
      // error.code: "missing_headers" | "timestamp_out_of_range" | "invalid_signature" | "invalid_payload"
      return new Response(error.message, { status: error.code === "invalid_payload" ? 400 : 401 });
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

Test a handler locally without forwarding: `sendTo` with the `standard-webhooks` provider signs the body with the given secret and sends `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature`, which `verifyForwardedEmail` accepts (the `webhook-id` is random rather than derived from the email's id):

```typescript
await client.sendTo("http://localhost:3000/hooks/email", {
  provider: "standard-webhooks",
  secret: process.env.FORWARD_SECRET!,
  body: client.emails.toJson(email),
});
```

### Send to Arbitrary URLs

```typescript
// Send webhook to any URL (not just your endpoints)
const response = await client.sendTo("https://example.com/webhook", {
  method?: string,
  headers?: Record<string, string>,
  body?: unknown,
  provider?: string,        // For signed payloads
  secret?: string,
  event?: string,
});

// Preview without sending
const preview = await client.buildRequest("https://example.com/webhook", { ... });
// Returns: { url, method, headers, body }
```

### Usage

```typescript
const usage = await client.usage();
// Returns: { used, limit, remaining, plan: "free"|"pro"|"business", periodEnd }
```

### Sharing Localhost

```typescript
// Previews (whk share) and live tunnels (whk tunnel --live), with data and plan limits
const { shares, usage, limits } = await client.shares.list({ state: "live" });
await client.shares.stop(shares[0].id);
const { requests } = await client.shares.requests(shares[0].id); // visitor log, no addresses

// Share a local port by running the whk CLI (Node.js; whk on the PATH)
const preview = await client.shares.start({ port: 3000 });
console.log(preview.url); // https://sample-preview-1234-free.sharehooks.cc
await preview.stop();

// Reserved names (Pro and Business): <name>.sharehooks.cc
await client.names.reserve("acme-demo");           // { team } keeps it inside a team
await client.names.setPassword("acme-demo", "a long passphrase");
await client.names.clearPassword("acme-demo");
await client.names.release("acme-demo");
const { names, limit, used, teams } = await client.names.list();
```

`share()` (exported) does the same without a client. Requests captured while `whk tunnel --live` ran carry `liveResponse`: `{ status, headers, body, bodyTruncated, bodyEncoding, ms, outcome }`, what the local app answered and the sender got.

### Matchers

All matchers return `(request: Request) => boolean` for use with `waitFor` and `waitForAll`:

```typescript
import {
  matchMethod,      // matchMethod("POST")
  matchHeader,      // matchHeader("stripe-signature") or matchHeader("content-type", "application/json")
  matchPath,        // matchPath("/api/**"), glob wildcards
  matchQueryParam,  // matchQueryParam("token", "abc")
  matchBodyPath,    // matchBodyPath("data.object.id", "cs_123"), dot-notation
  matchBodySubset,  // matchBodySubset({ type: "checkout.session.completed" })
  matchContentType, // matchContentType("application/json")
  matchAll,         // matchAll(matchMethod("POST"), matchHeader("stripe-signature"))
  matchAny,         // matchAny(matchMethod("POST"), matchMethod("PUT"))
  matchEmail,       // matchEmail({ tag: "run-42", subject: "Confirm" }), same criteria as client.emails
  isEmailRequest,   // isEmailRequest(request): type guard for a captured email with its parsed message
} from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";
```

### Provider Detection Helpers

```typescript
import {
  isStripeWebhook,     // Checks stripe-signature header
  isGitHubWebhook,     // Checks x-github-event header
  isShopifyWebhook,    // Checks x-shopify-hmac-sha256 header
  isSlackWebhook,      // Checks x-slack-signature header
  isTwilioWebhook,     // Checks x-twilio-signature header
  isPaddleWebhook,     // Checks paddle-signature header
  isLinearWebhook,     // Checks linear-signature header
  isDiscordWebhook,    // Checks x-signature-ed25519 + x-signature-timestamp
  isSendGridWebhook,   // Checks body for sg_event_id
  isClerkWebhook,      // Checks svix-id header
  isVercelWebhook,     // Checks x-vercel-signature header
  isGitLabWebhook,     // Checks x-gitlab-event or x-gitlab-token header
  isStandardWebhook,   // Checks svix-id header (Polar, Svix, Clerk, Resend)
} from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";
```

There is one for each of the other providers too: `isTypeformWebhook`, `isMetaWebhook`, `isLemonSqueezyWebhook`, `isCoinbaseCommerceWebhook`, `isRazorpayWebhook`, `isCalWebhook`, `isIntercomWebhook`, `isTelegramWebhook`, `isSquareWebhook`, `isHubSpotWebhook`, `isMailgunWebhook`, `isCalendlyWebhook`, `isMuxWebhook`, `isSentryWebhook`, `isBitbucketWebhook`, `isDocuSignWebhook`, `isAdyenWebhook`, `isPayPalWebhook`, `isPlaidWebhook`, `isResendWebhook` and `isWorkOSWebhook`.

### Body Parsing Helpers

```typescript
import {
  parseJsonBody,      // parseJsonBody(request) → parsed JSON or undefined
  parseFormBody,       // parseFormBody(request) → Record<string, string | string[]>
  parseBody,           // Auto-detect content-type and parse
  extractJsonField,    // extractJsonField<T>(request, "data.object.id")
  matchJsonField,      // matchJsonField("event", "invoice.paid"), returns matcher
} from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";
```

### Error Classes

```typescript
import {
  WebhooksCCError,    // Base error (statusCode, message)
  UnauthorizedError,  // 401: invalid/missing API key
  NotFoundError,      // 404: resource not found
  TimeoutError,       // Request timeout
  RateLimitError,     // 429: includes retryAfter, limit, remaining, reset
  ApiError,           // General API error
  WebhookVerificationError,  // From verifyForwardedEmail(); `code` says which check failed
} from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";
```

### Type Definitions

```typescript
interface Endpoint {
  id: string;
  slug: string;
  name?: string;
  url?: string;
  notificationUrl?: string;
  isEphemeral?: boolean;
  expiresAt?: number;       // Unix ms
  createdAt: number;        // Unix ms
  responseRules?: ResponseRule[];  // Conditional response rules
  sharedWith?: TeamShare[];
  fromTeam?: TeamShare;
  emailAddress?: string | null;  // null for guest endpoints
  showEmailExtracts?: boolean;
  forwardEnabled?: boolean;
  forwardUrl?: string | null;    // owner only
  hasForwardSecret?: boolean;
}

interface Request {
  id: string;
  endpointId: string;
  method: string;
  path: string;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  body?: string;
  bodyRaw?: string;         // Base64-encoded raw bytes
  queryParams: Record<string, string>;
  contentType?: string;
  ip: string;
  size: number;             // Bytes
  receivedAt: number;       // Unix ms
  kind?: "http" | "email";
  email?: EmailCapture | null;  // Parsed message, for a captured email (see Email Capture)
  liveResponse?: LiveResponse | null;  // What the local app answered, under whk tunnel --live
}

interface EmailRequest extends Request {
  kind: "email";
  email: EmailCapture;
}

interface MockResponse {
  status: number;           // 100-599
  body: string;
  headers: Record<string, string>;
  delay?: number;           // 0-30000ms
}

interface UsageInfo {
  used: number;
  limit: number;
  remaining: number;
  plan: "free" | "pro" | "business";
  periodEnd: number | null;
}
```

### SDK Quick Start Example

```typescript
import { WebhooksCC, matchAll, matchMethod, matchBodyPath } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

const client = new WebhooksCC({ apiKey: process.env.WHK_API_KEY! });

// Create an endpoint
const endpoint = await client.endpoints.create({ name: "stripe-test" });
console.log(endpoint.url); // https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>

// Send a signed Stripe webhook
await client.endpoints.sendTemplate(endpoint.slug, {
  provider: "stripe",
  secret: "whsec_test_secret",
  event: "checkout.session.completed",
});

// Wait for it
const request = await client.requests.waitFor(endpoint.slug, {
  timeout: "30s",
  match: matchAll(
    matchMethod("POST"),
    matchBodyPath("type", "checkout.session.completed"),
  ),
});

console.log(request.headers["stripe-signature"]);

// Clean up
await client.endpoints.delete(endpoint.slug);
```

---

## MCP Server Reference

Remote server: https://webhooks.cc/mcp (streamable HTTP, OAuth). Local server: the `@webhooks-cc/mcp` package on npm.

### Installation

**Remote server (recommended).** Any client that can add a remote MCP server uses it: coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex) as well as claude.ai and ChatGPT. There is no key and nothing to install: the first time the client connects, the human signs in to webhooks.cc in the browser and clicks Connect. There is no code to type and nothing expires after 24 hours; the connection lasts until it goes unused for 90 days or is disconnected under Account, Connected agents.

```bash
# Claude Code (then /mcp in Claude Code to sign in)
claude mcp add -s user --transport http webhooks-cc https://webhooks.cc/mcp

# Codex (opens the browser to sign in)
codex mcp add webhooks-cc --url https://webhooks.cc/mcp
```

Cursor, in `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "webhooks-cc": { "url": "https://webhooks.cc/mcp" } } }
```

VS Code, in `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{ "servers": { "webhooks-cc": { "type": "http", "url": "https://webhooks.cc/mcp" } } }
```

claude.ai and Claude Desktop: in Settings, Connectors, add a custom connector with the URL `https://webhooks.cc/mcp`. ChatGPT: add it as a custom connector (in developer mode).

The remote server has every tool below except `send_to` and `replay_request`, which post to a URL on your machine that a hosted server cannot reach (for the same reason `render_email` and `test_webhook_flow` refuse `targetUrl`). Waits are capped at 50 seconds, it has no prompts or resources, and it needs an account: a sandbox token is refused. Full setup: https://webhooks.cc/docs/mcp#remote-server.

**Local server.** Use it to send to localhost, for its prompts and resources, without an account (it starts in the agent sandbox), or in CI with an API key.

```bash
# Claude Code
claude mcp add webhooks-cc -- npx -y @webhooks-cc/mcp

# Cursor / VS Code / Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
npx @webhooks-cc/mcp setup cursor
npx @webhooks-cc/mcp setup vscode
npx @webhooks-cc/mcp setup devin

# Codex
codex mcp add webhooks-cc -- npx -y @webhooks-cc/mcp
```

`WHK_API_KEY` is optional. Without it the local server starts connected to the account the agent was connected to before (saved in ~/.config/whk/agent.json), or in the keyless agent sandbox: 3 endpoints for 24 hours, and `connect_account` then `wait_for_connection` connect a human's account. See https://webhooks.cc/auth.md.

### MCP Tools

The local server has 57 tools once it is connected to an account; the remote server has the same tools except `send_to`, `replay_request` and `share_port` (54). In the keyless sandbox the local server offers a smaller set, with `connect_account` and `wait_for_connection` to connect a human's account. `describe` returns every tool's parameters.

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| `create_endpoint` | name?, ephemeral?, expiresIn?, mockResponse?, responseRules?, notificationUrl?, site?, signingProvider?, signingSecret?, signingHeader? | Create a new webhook endpoint |
| `list_endpoints` | team? | List your endpoints and those shared with you through teams |
| `get_endpoint` | slug | Get endpoint details |
| `favorite_endpoint` | slug, favorite? (default true) | Mark or unmark one of your favourite endpoints |
| `update_endpoint` | slug, name?, mockResponse?, responseRules?, notificationUrl?, signingProvider?, signingSecret?, signingHeader?, showEmailExtracts?, site?, emailFields?, layouts? | Update endpoint config |
| `preview_layouts` | slug, requestId?, layouts? | Dry run of an endpoint's layouts on a captured email; no pages used |
| `preview_response` | slug, requestId?, mockResponse?, responseRules? | Which response rule answers a captured request, with placeholders filled in |
| `delete_endpoint` | slug | Delete endpoint |
| `create_endpoints` | count (1-20), namePrefix?, ephemeral?, expiresIn? | Bulk create endpoints |
| `delete_endpoints` | slugs (array, 1-100) | Bulk delete endpoints |
| `list_teams` | (none) | Teams you own or belong to, with seats and pooled usage |
| `list_team_members` | teamId | A team's members and pending invites |
| `share_endpoint` | slug, teamId | Share an endpoint you own with a team |
| `unshare_endpoint` | slug, teamId | Stop sharing an endpoint with a team |
| `send_webhook` | slug, method?, headers?, body?, provider?, template?, event?, secret? | Send test webhook |
| `list_requests` | endpointSlug, limit (1-100), since?, kind? | List recent requests |
| `search_requests` | slug?, method?, kind?, q?, from?, to?, limit, offset, order | Search request history |
| `count_requests` | slug?, method?, kind?, q?, from?, to? | Count matching requests |
| `get_request` | requestId | Get single request |
| `wait_for_request` | endpointSlug, timeout?, pollInterval? | Wait for next request |
| `wait_for_requests` | endpointSlug, count (1-20), timeout?, pollInterval?, method? | Collect N requests |
| `replay_request` | requestId, targetUrl | Replay request to URL (local server only) |
| `compare_requests` | leftRequestId, rightRequestId, ignoreHeaders? | Diff two requests |
| `generate_payload_schema` | endpointSlug, format?, name?, event?, method?, path?, requestIds?, limit? | TypeScript, Zod, Pydantic, or JSON Schema from captured bodies |
| `extract_from_request` | requestId, jsonPaths (1-50) | Extract JSON fields |
| `verify_signature` | requestId, provider?, secret?, publicKey?, url?, method? | Verify webhook signature |
| `clear_requests` | slug, before? | Delete captured requests |
| `send_to` | url, method?, headers?, body?, provider?, template?, event?, secret? | Send to any URL (local server only) |
| `preview_webhook` | url, method?, headers?, body?, provider?, template?, event?, secret? | Preview without sending |
| `list_provider_templates` | provider? | List providers/templates |
| `get_usage` | (none) | Usage and quota, with each subscribed team's pool |
| `test_webhook_flow` | provider?, event?, secret?, mockStatus?, targetUrl?, verifySignature?, cleanup? | Full end-to-end test flow |
| `list_emails` | endpointSlug, limit?, since?, tag?, subject?, from? | Emails an endpoint received, with codes and links |
| `get_email` | requestId? or endpointSlug (+ tag?), includeHtml? | One captured email |
| `wait_for_email` | endpointSlug, tag?, subject?, from?, timeout?, since?, includeHtml? | Wait for an email, then return its code and link |
| `send_test_email` | slug, tag? | Deliver a sample email to an endpoint |
| `render_email` | requestId, format, mailgunSigningKey?, targetUrl? | An email in Postmark, SendGrid, Mailgun or CloudMailin's inbound shape |
| `list_destinations` | slug, summary? | Where an endpoint's captures go (owner only) |
| `add_destination` | slug, url, name?, enabled?, http?, email?, filter?, format?, bodyTemplate?, messageTemplate?, headers?, throttleSeconds?, delaySeconds?, ... | Add a destination (up to 10 per endpoint) |
| `update_destination` | slug, destinationId, url?, and any destination field | Change a destination |
| `remove_destination` | slug, destinationId | Remove a destination |
| `preview_destination` | slug, destinationId? or destination, requestId? | Dry run: does the filter pass, and the exact request it would send |
| `configure_forwarding` | slug, url?, enabled?, http?, email?, format?, headers?, appendPath?, retrySeconds?, keepOrder?, sentField? | Change the endpoint's primary destination |
| `get_forwarding_secret` | slug, destinationId?, rotate? | Read or rotate a destination's whsec_ secret |
| `test_forwarding` | slug, destinationId?, kind?, requestId? | Send one delivery now and report the answer |
| `list_deliveries` | endpointSlug? or requestId, limit?, status?, destinationId?, before? | The delivery log, or every try of one request |
| `redeliver` | requestId? or endpointSlug, destinationId? | Forward again with the current settings |
| `share_port` | port, name?, password? | Share a local port at https://<name>.sharehooks.cc by running whk share (local server only) |
| `list_shares` | state? (live, ended) | Previews and live tunnels, with this month's shared data and the plan's sharing limits |
| `stop_share` | id | Stop a preview or live tunnel; its CLI is told why and exits |
| `share_requests` | id | The last requests visitors made to a running preview (no addresses) |
| `list_names` | (none) | Reserved preview names, your own and your teams', with the plan's count |
| `reserve_name` | name, team? | Reserve a preview name (Pro and Business), optionally inside a team |
| `release_name` | name | Let a reserved name go; a preview under it stops |
| `set_name_password` | name, password | Put a password on every preview under a name |
| `clear_name_password` | name | Remove a name's password |
| `describe` | (none) | Get SDK schema introspection |

### Supported Providers for Signed Webhooks

34 providers: Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, Twilio, Slack, Paddle, Linear, SendGrid, Clerk, Discord, Vercel, GitLab, Typeform, Standard Webhooks, Meta, Lemon Squeezy, Coinbase Commerce, Razorpay, Cal.com, Intercom, Telegram, Square, HubSpot, Mailgun, Calendly, Mux, Sentry, Bitbucket, DocuSign, Adyen, PayPal, Plaid, Resend and WorkOS. Signature verification covers all of them except SendGrid and Plaid, which have templates only.

Each signed template uses the provider's native algorithm (HMAC-SHA256, Ed25519, etc.) so your handler verification code works identically to production.

---

## CLI Reference

Binary: `whk`. Install via Homebrew, the install script, or GitHub releases.

```bash
brew install kroqdotdev/tap/whk
# or
curl -fsSL https://webhooks.cc/install.sh | sh
# without root: any directory you can write to (created when missing)
curl -fsSL https://webhooks.cc/install.sh | WHK_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin" sh
```

### Global Flags

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--nogui` | Disable TUI mode |
| `--json` | Output as JSON |
| `--api-url <url>` | Override API URL (env: WHK_API_URL) |
| `--webhook-url <url>` | Override receiver URL (env: WHK_WEBHOOK_URL) |
| `--no-color` | Disable colored output |

### Commands

```bash
whk                                    # Interactive TUI dashboard

# Authentication
whk auth login                         # Browser-based device auth
whk auth status                        # Show login status
whk auth logout                        # Clear stored token

# Endpoint management
whk create [name]                      # Create endpoint
  --ephemeral / -e                     # Auto-expire
  --expires-in <duration>              # e.g. "12h"
  --mock-status <code>                 # Mock response status
  --mock-body <text>                   # Mock response body
  --mock-header KEY:VALUE              # Mock header (repeatable)

whk list                               # List endpoints
whk get <slug>                         # Get endpoint details
whk favorite <slug>                    # Mark a favourite (whk unfavorite <slug> undoes it)
whk delete <slug> [--force/-f]         # Delete endpoint

whk update-endpoint <slug>             # Update endpoint
  --name <text>
  --mock-status <code>
  --mock-body <text>
  --mock-header KEY:VALUE
  --clear-mock

# Tunneling and streaming
whk tunnel <port>[/path]               # Forward webhooks to localhost
  --endpoint <slug>                    # Reuse existing endpoint
  --ephemeral / -e                     # Delete on exit
  -H, --header KEY:VALUE              # Custom forwarding headers
  --email-format <format>              # json (default), postmark, sendgrid, mailgun or cloudmailin
  --email-path <path> / --no-email     # Where emails go, or skip them
  --live                               # Relay each webhook while the sender waits; the sender gets your app's answer
                                       # (502 when whk is not connected, 504 after 25 s), stored with the request

whk listen <slug>                      # Stream requests to terminal

# Sharing localhost (https://webhooks.cc/docs/share)
whk share <port>                       # Public link https://<name>.sharehooks.cc to a local site
  --name <name>                        # A name you reserved (paid plans); random otherwise (Free: ends in -free)
  --password                           # Visitors need a password (prompted or WHK_SHARE_PASSWORD; paid plans)
  --no-qr / --json                     # No QR code / one JSON event per line
whk shares ls [--ended] | stop <id|name> | log <id|name>   # log: the last requests visitors made, no addresses
whk names ls | reserve <name> | release <name> | password <name> [--clear]

# Sending and replaying
whk send <slug>                        # Send test webhook
  --method <method>
  -H, --header KEY:VALUE
  -d, --data <string|@file>

whk send-to <url>                      # Send to any URL
  --method <method>
  -H, --header KEY:VALUE
  -d, --data <string|@file>

whk replay <id>                        # Replay captured request
  --to <url>                           # Default: http://localhost:8080

# Request management
whk requests list <slug>               # List requests
  --limit <n> --since <ts> --cursor <c>

whk requests get <id>                  # Get single request
whk requests search                    # Search requests
  --slug --method -q --from --to --limit --offset --order

whk requests count                     # Count matching requests
whk requests clear <slug> [--force]    # Delete requests
whk requests export <slug>             # Export requests
  --format har|curl --limit <n> -o <file>

# Teams
whk teams list|members|share|unshare|invite|invites|accept|decline

# Agent sandbox (no account)
whk sandbox create|list|get|delete|requests|request|wait|status|connect|forget

# Other
whk usage                              # Show quota info
whk update                             # Self-update (SHA256 verified)
whk completions <shell>                # Generate shell completions
```

Config stored at `~/.config/whk/token.json`.

---

## REST API Reference

Base URL: `https://webhooks.cc`

Docs: https://webhooks.cc/docs/api. OpenAPI 3.1 document with every route below, its parameters and its response shapes: https://webhooks.cc/openapi.yaml

All endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer whcc_...` unless noted. "Bearer" is an API key, an OAuth access token or an agent's access token (all `whcc_` tokens). "Session" routes take only a signed-in browser session and answer `403` to an API key. "Owner" routes answer `404` to anyone but the endpoint's owner. Bodies and responses are JSON; timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Errors are `{ "error": "..." }` with `400` (validation), `401` (missing or invalid token), `403` (not allowed), `404`, `409` (conflict), `429` (rate limited, with `Retry-After`) or `500`.

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/endpoints` | Bearer | List endpoints: `{ "owned": [...], "shared": [...] }` |
| POST | `/api/endpoints` | Bearer | Create endpoint; body `{ "name"?, "isEphemeral"?, "expiresAt"?, "mockResponse"?, "responseRules"?, "notificationUrl"?, "site"? }` (rate limit: 30 per 10 min) |
| GET | `/api/endpoints/[slug]` | Bearer | Get endpoint |
| PATCH | `/api/endpoints/[slug]` | Bearer | Update endpoint: `name`, `mockResponse`, `responseRules` (team members too), and for the owner `notificationUrl`, `showEmailExtracts`, `site`, `emailFields`, `layouts`, `retentionDays`, `deleteAfterDelivery`, `signingProvider`, `signingSecret`, `signingHeader` and the `forward*` fields |
| DELETE | `/api/endpoints/[slug]` | Bearer | Delete endpoint and its requests |
| PUT/DELETE | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/favorite` | Bearer | Mark or unmark it as your favourite: `{ "favorite": true }` |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/claim` | Bearer | Claim a guest endpoint into your account; body `{ "slug": "..." }` |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/responses/preview` | Bearer | Dry run of the response rules on a captured request; body `{ "requestId"?, "mockResponse"?, "responseRules"? }`; returns `{ "rule", "response", "unknownPlaceholders", "email", "request" }` |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/email-fields/preview` | Bearer, owner | Dry run of named email fields; body `{ "requestId"?, "emailFields"? }`; returns `{ "problems", "request", "values" }` |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/layouts/preview` | Bearer, owner | Dry run of layouts on a captured email; body `{ "requestId"?, "layouts"? }`; returns `{ "problems", "layoutsCap", "request", "parsed" }`; uses no pages |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/layouts/template` | Bearer, owner | Add a ready-made layout; body `{ "template": "shopify-orders" }`; returns `201` `{ "layoutId": "..." }` |
| GET/PUT | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/alerts` | Bearer, owner | Read `{ "settings", "events" }` or change the alert settings |

### Requests

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/requests` | Bearer | List requests, newest first (`limit`, `since`, `kind=http\|email`, `extracts=true`) |
| GET | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/requests/paginated` | Bearer | The same page by page (`limit`, `cursor`, `kind`, `extracts`): `{ "items", "cursor", "hasMore" }` |
| DELETE | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/requests` | Bearer | Clear requests (`before=<ms>` for older ones only); `204` |
| GET | `/api/requests/[id]` | Bearer | Get single request (`extracts=true` adds an email's codes, links, named fields and reply text) |
| GET | `/api/requests/[id]/raw` | Bearer | A captured email's exact message as `message/rfc822` |
| GET | `/api/requests/[id]/attachments/[index]` | Bearer | One attachment of a stored email, as a download |
| POST | `/api/requests/[id]/render` | Bearer | A captured email as an inbound mail provider posts it; body `{ "format": "postmark" \| "sendgrid" \| "mailgun" \| "cloudmailin" \| "json" }`; returns `{ "format", "method", "headers", "body" }` |
| GET | `/api/search/requests` | Bearer | Search requests (`slug`, `method`, `kind`, `q`, `from`, `to`, `limit`, `offset`, `order`) |
| GET | `/api/search/requests/count` | Bearer | Count matching requests: `{ "count": 42 }` |

### Webhooks

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/api/send-test` | Bearer | Send test webhook; body `{ "slug", "method", "path"?, "headers"?, "body"? }` (rate limit: 30/min) |
| POST | `/api/send-test-email` | Bearer | Deliver a sample email to an endpoint, body `{ "slug": "...", "tag": "..." }` with `tag` optional (rate limit: 10/min) |

### Forwarding

Forwarding settings are owner only. The owner-only routes below answer `404` to anyone else. Destinations are the current API; the `forward*` endpoint fields and the `/forwarding` routes are the older single-URL API, which still works and stands for the endpoint's primary destination.

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET/POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/destinations` | Bearer, owner | List (`?summary=true` adds each one's last 24 hours) or add destinations (up to 10; `201`) |
| GET/PATCH/DELETE | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/destinations/[id]` | Bearer, owner | Read, change or remove one destination |
| GET/POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/destinations/[id]/secret` | Bearer, owner | Read or rotate a destination's signing secret: `{ "secret": "whsec_..." }` |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/destinations/[id]/test` | Bearer, owner | Send one delivery now and report the answer; body `{ "kind"?, "requestId"? }` (rate limit: 10/min) |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/destinations/preview` | Bearer, owner | Dry run: body `{ "destinationId"?, "destination"?, "requestId"? }`; returns the exact request it would send, nothing is sent |
| PUT | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/destinations/order` | Bearer, owner | Reorder destinations; body `{ "ids": [...] }` |
| GET | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/deliveries` | Bearer, owner | The delivery log, newest first: `limit` 1 to 100 (default 5), `status` (`all`, `pending`, `failed`, `skipped`), `destination` (an id), `before` (a row's `cursor`) |
| GET | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/deliveries/summary` | Bearer, owner | Counts: `{ "last24h": { "delivered", "failed" }, "pending", "failed", "total" }` |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/deliveries/redeliver-failed` | Bearer, owner | Queue every failed delivery again (`?destination=<id>` for one): `{ "queued": 12 }` (rate limit: 10/min) |
| GET | `/api/requests/[id]/deliveries` | Bearer | Deliveries of one request with every attempt; anyone who can read the request |
| POST | `/api/requests/[id]/deliveries` | Bearer, owner | Redeliver the request (HTTP or email) to every destination that takes it, or body `{ "destinationId": "..." }` for one; `409` when none takes it (rate limit: 30/min) |
| POST | `/api/requests/[id]/replay` | Bearer, owner | Read the request again (layouts included) and send it through the destinations: `{ "queued": true }` (rate limit: 60/min) |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/replay` | Bearer, owner | The same for a time range; body `{ "since"?, "until"?, "kind"? }` in ms, at most 500 requests: `{ "requests", "queued", "limit" }` (rate limit: 10/min) |
| GET | `/api/integrations/google/connections` | Bearer | Connected Google accounts for Sheets destinations: `{ "available", "connections" }` |
| PATCH | `/api/endpoints/[slug]` | Bearer, owner | Legacy: set `forwardUrl`, `forwardEnabled` and the other `forward*` fields of the primary destination (team members get `403`) |
| GET/POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/forwarding` | Bearer, owner | Legacy: read or rotate the primary destination's signing secret |
| POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/forwarding/test` | Bearer, owner | Legacy: send the newest request (or a sample) to the primary destination once and report the answer (rate limit: 10/min) |

### Streaming

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/stream/[slug]` | Bearer | SSE stream of incoming requests (`connected`, `request`, `timeout`, `endpoint_deleted` events; 30 minutes at most) |

### Auth (Device Flow for CLI)

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/api/auth/device-code` | None | Create device code |
| POST | `/api/auth/device-authorize` | Session | Authorize device |
| GET | `/api/auth/device-poll?code=<device code>` | None | Poll until the device code is authorized |
| POST | `/api/auth/device-claim` | None | Exchange an authorized device code for an API key; body `{ "deviceCode": "..." }` |

Agents without a human at hand register through `/api/agent/identity` and exchange the assertion at `/api/oauth2/token`; see https://webhooks.cc/auth.md.

### Account

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/usage` | Bearer | Usage and quota: `{ "used", "limit", "remaining", "blockRequests", "creditRequests", "overage", "plan", "periodEnd", "teamBilledEndpoints", "emails" }` |
| GET/POST/DELETE | `/api/api-keys` | Session | List, create or delete API keys |
| PATCH/DELETE | `/api/account` | Session | Change account settings, or delete the account |
| * | `/api/billing/*`, `/api/teams/[id]/billing/*` | Session | Plans, seats, extra capacity, checkout and cancellation |
| * | `/api/domains`, `/api/domains/[id]`, `/api/domains/[id]/verify` | Session | Custom inbound domains (Business) |
| * | `/api/requests/[id]/shares`, `/api/request-shares` | Session | Share links |
| GET/POST | `/api/endpoints/[slug]/layouts/assist` | Session | AI setup for layouts and fields |

### Teams

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/teams` | Bearer | List teams |
| POST | `/api/teams` | Bearer | Create team; body `{ "name": "..." }` |
| PATCH/DELETE | `/api/teams/[id]` | Bearer | Rename or delete a team (owner) |
| GET | `/api/teams/[id]/members` | Bearer | Members and pending invites |
| DELETE | `/api/teams/[id]/members/[userId]` | Bearer | Remove a member (owner) |
| GET | `/api/teams/[id]/endpoints` | Bearer | Endpoints shared with the team: `{ "endpoints": [...] }` |
| POST | `/api/teams/[id]/endpoints` | Bearer | Share one of your endpoints; body `{ "endpointId": "..." }` |
| DELETE | `/api/teams/[id]/endpoints/[endpointId]` | Bearer | Unshare an endpoint |
| POST | `/api/teams/[id]/invite` | Bearer | Invite by email (owner); body `{ "email": "..." }` |
| DELETE | `/api/teams/[id]/invites/[inviteId]` | Bearer | Revoke a pending invite (owner) |
| POST | `/api/teams/[id]/leave` | Bearer | Leave a team |
| GET | `/api/invites` | Bearer | Invites addressed to you |
| POST | `/api/invites/[id]/accept`, `/api/invites/[id]/decline` | Bearer | Accept or decline an invite |

### Sharing Localhost

API key, claimed agent token or session; 503 where sharing is not set up.

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/api/shares?state=live\|ended` | Bearer | Previews and live tunnels, this month's data, plan limits, names standing, `hints` (next steps as whk commands) |
| POST | `/api/shares/[id]/stop` | Bearer | Stop a preview or live tunnel (the CLI exits, saying why) |
| GET | `/api/shares/[id]/requests` | Bearer | A running preview's visitor log (no addresses) |
| GET | `/api/tunnel-names` | Bearer | Reserved names, own and team counts |
| POST | `/api/tunnel-names` | Bearer | Reserve a name; body `{ "name", "team"? }` |
| DELETE | `/api/tunnel-names/[name]` | Bearer | Release a name (stops a preview under it) |
| PUT/DELETE | `/api/tunnel-names/[name]/password` | Bearer | Set (`{ "password" }`, 8 to 200 characters) or clear a name's password |

### Guest (No Auth)

| Method | Path | Auth | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/api/go/endpoint` | None | Create ephemeral endpoint (IP rate limited; refuses crawler and missing user agents with `403`) |

---

## Conditional Response Rules

Endpoints can have an ordered list of conditional response rules. Each rule has match conditions and its own response (status, headers, body, delay). Rules are evaluated in order, and the first match wins. If no rule matches, the default `mockResponse` is returned. If no default exists, the endpoint returns 200 OK.

### Rule Structure

```typescript
interface ResponseRule {
  id?: string;                    // Stable ID for UI reordering
  name?: string;                  // Human-readable label (max 200 chars)
  enabled?: boolean;              // Default: true
  logic?: "and" | "or";          // How conditions combine (default: "and")
  conditions: ResponseRuleCondition[];  // 1-10 conditions per rule
  response: MockResponse;         // Status, body, headers, delay
}

interface ResponseRuleCondition {
  field: "method" | "path" | "header" | "body_contains" | "body_path" | "query";
  op: "eq" | "contains" | "starts_with" | "matches" | "exists";
  value?: string;                 // Required for non-"exists" ops (max 4096 chars)
  name?: string;                  // Required for header/query conditions (max 256 chars)
  path?: string;                  // Required for body_path conditions, dot-notation (max 256 chars)
}
```

### Condition Types

| Field | Operators | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| `method` | `eq` | HTTP method (case-insensitive) |
| `path` | `eq`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `matches` | Request path after slug. `matches` uses glob patterns (`*` = segment, `**` = any) |
| `header` | `exists`, `eq`, `contains` | Header lookup by `name` (case-insensitive) |
| `body_contains` | `contains` | Substring search in raw body |
| `body_path` | `exists`, `eq`, `contains` | JSON dot-notation path (e.g. `data.object.id`, `items.0.name`) |
| `query` | `exists`, `eq` | Query parameter lookup by `name` |

### Limits

- Max 50 rules per endpoint
- Max 10 conditions per rule
- Glob patterns max 500 chars
- Body JSON parsing is lazy: only triggered when a `body_path` condition exists

### SDK Usage

```typescript
// Create endpoint with conditional rules
const endpoint = await client.endpoints.create({
  name: "multi-provider",
  responseRules: [
    {
      name: "Stripe invoices",
      logic: "and",
      conditions: [
        { field: "header", op: "exists", name: "stripe-signature" },
        { field: "body_path", op: "eq", path: "type", value: "invoice.paid" },
      ],
      response: { status: 200, body: '{"received": true}', headers: { "content-type": "application/json" } },
    },
    {
      name: "GitHub pushes",
      conditions: [
        { field: "header", op: "eq", name: "x-github-event", value: "push" },
      ],
      response: { status: 202, body: "accepted", headers: {} },
    },
    {
      name: "Any PUT or PATCH",
      logic: "or",
      conditions: [
        { field: "method", op: "eq", value: "PUT" },
        { field: "method", op: "eq", value: "PATCH" },
      ],
      response: { status: 204, body: "", headers: {} },
    },
  ],
  mockResponse: { status: 200, body: "ok", headers: {} }, // default fallback
});

// Update rules on existing endpoint
await client.endpoints.update("my-slug", {
  responseRules: [/* new rules */],
});

// Clear all rules
await client.endpoints.update("my-slug", {
  responseRules: null,
});
```

### MCP Usage

The `create_endpoint` and `update_endpoint` MCP tools accept `responseRules` with the same schema. Pass `responseRules: null` to clear rules.

### Dashboard

The endpoint settings dialog includes a visual rule editor with:
- Drag-to-reorder rules (first match wins)
- Enable/disable toggle per rule
- AND/OR logic selector
- Condition builder with field-aware operator and input dropdowns
- Per-rule response configuration (status, headers, body, delay)
- Default response section below rules

### Evaluation Flow

1. Webhook arrives at receiver
2. `capture_webhook()` returns rules + default mock from Postgres
3. Rust receiver evaluates rules in order (first match wins)
4. If no rule matches, default `mockResponse` is used
5. If no default exists, returns 200 OK

---

## Webhook Capture Details

Any HTTP method, content type, and body up to 1 MB is accepted at `https://go.webhooks.cc/w/<slug>`.

Captured data per request:
- HTTP method
- Path (after slug)
- All headers (proxy headers filtered)
- Body (text)
- Query parameters
- Content-Type
- Client IP
- Received timestamp
- Body size in bytes

Mock responses can return custom status codes (100-599), headers, body, and an optional delay (0-30 seconds). Conditional response rules allow different responses based on request properties (method, path, headers, body content, JSON paths, query params). The first matching rule wins, with fallback to the default mock response.

When the database has a transient problem, the receiver answers `503` with `Retry-After: 5` so senders retry. Permanent errors fail open with `200 OK`.

---

## Email Capture

Docs: https://webhooks.cc/docs/email-capture

Every endpoint that belongs to an account receives email at `<slug>@mailhooks.cc`, on every plan, including endpoints shared with a team. Add a tag after a plus sign (`<slug>+signup@mailhooks.cc`) to tell test runs or flows apart: tagged mail lands on the same endpoint and the tag is kept on the email. The slug is not case sensitive; the tag is kept exactly as written. Guest endpoints (created without an account) receive no email, because anyone who knows a guest slug can read what it captured. The address is in each endpoint's `emailAddress` field (`null` for guest endpoints).

An email is stored as an ordinary request, in the same list as webhooks:

- `kind`: `"email"` (`"http"` for everything else)
- `method`: `"EMAIL"`
- `path`: the recipient address
- `body`: the original message, or only its headers when the message is over 1 MB
- `headers`: the message headers
- `contentType`: `message/rfc822`
- `ip`: the sending mail server's IP address
- `email`: the parsed message (below)

```typescript
// The `email` field of GET /api/requests/{id}, the request list routes, and search results
interface EmailCapture {
  subject: string | null;
  from: EmailAddress[];
  to: EmailAddress[];
  cc: EmailAddress[];
  replyTo: EmailAddress[];
  sender: EmailAddress[];
  date: string | null;             // the Date header as RFC 3339
  messageId: string | null;
  inReplyTo: string[];
  tag: string | null;              // the +tag of the address
  text: string | null;             // up to 256 KB
  html: string | null;             // up to 256 KB
  textFromHtml: boolean;           // no text part, so text was derived from the HTML
  attachments: {                   // contents downloadable from /api/attachments
    filename: string | null;
    contentType: string;
    size: number;
    contentId: string | null;
    inline: boolean;
  }[];
  auth: {                          // sender checks run when the message arrived
    spf: { result: string; domain: string | null } | null;
    dkim: { result: string; domain: string | null; selector: string | null }[];
    dmarc: { result: string; domain: string | null; policy: string | null; reason: string | null } | null;
    iprev: { result: string; ptr: string | null } | null;   // reverse DNS
    authenticationResults: string | null;
    error: string | null;          // set when the checks could not run
  } | null;
  smtp: {
    clientIp: string | null;
    clientRdns: string | null;
    helo: string | null;
    tls: { version: string | null; cipher: string | null } | null;
    envelopeFrom: string | null;
    envelopeTo: string[];
    size: number | null;           // whole message in bytes
    test: boolean;                 // the dashboard's "Send test email" sample
  } | null;
  parseError: boolean;             // unparseable; the original is still in body
  truncated: {
    raw: boolean;                  // over 1 MB, body holds the headers only
    text: boolean;
    html: boolean;
    headers: boolean;
    addresses: boolean;
    attachments: boolean;
  };
}

interface EmailAddress {
  name: string | null;
  address: string | null;
}
```

Check results are strings such as `pass`, `fail`, `softfail`, `neutral`, `none`, `temperror` and `permerror`. Failing a check does not stop a message from being captured.

Finding emails through the API:

- `GET /api/endpoints/<slug>/requests?kind=email` (also on `/requests/paginated`) and `GET /api/search/requests?kind=email` (or `method=EMAIL`) return only emails; `kind=http` only webhooks.
- The SSE stream (`/api/stream/<slug>`) sends emails as `request` events with `kind: "email"` and `method: "EMAIL"`, without `email`, and names the request id `_id`. Fetch the request by that id for the parsed message.
- `POST /api/send-test-email` with `{ "slug": "<slug>" }` delivers a sample message with a six-digit code and a link; add `"tag": "<tag>"` to send it to `<slug>+<tag>@mailhooks.cc`. It counts as one request and does not travel over SMTP, so no sender checks run on it.
- In the SDK: `client.emails` (see TypeScript SDK Reference above).

Limits and SMTP replies:

- An email counts as one request against the same quota as webhooks, once per endpoint it is addressed to. A sender's retry after a temporary failure is captured once; sending the same message again on purpose captures it again.
- Messages up to 10 MB, up to 20 recipients per message.
- `250` captured; `550 5.1.1` no endpoint with that slug; `550 5.7.1` guest endpoint; `552 5.2.2` request quota used up; `552 5.3.4` message over 10 MB; `452` for recipients past the 20th; `451` temporary problem, the sender retries.
- Emails follow the plan's retention, like HTTP requests.
- `mailhooks.cc` only receives. It never sends mail, replies, or bounces of its own.
- Notification URLs fire for emails too, with `"method": "EMAIL"` and the recipient address as `path`.

---

## Forwarding (Destinations)

Docs: https://webhooks.cc/docs/forwarding

Forwarding sends what an endpoint captures, HTTP requests and emails, to up to 10 destinations, usually within a second or two. Each destination has its own kinds (`http`, `email`), filter, format, headers, timing and `whsec_` signing secret. Only the endpoint's owner can configure forwarding. It is available on every plan (file drops need Business) and does not use request quota (each request already counted once when it arrived).

### Set up

```bash
# Add a destination (its signing secret is created with it)
curl -X POST https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug>/destinations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url": "https://example.com/hooks/email", "http": false, "email": true, "format": "json"}'
# 201 {"id": "<destination id>", "url": "https://example.com/hooks/email", "enabled": true, "hasSecret": true, ...}

# Read the signing secret for your handler
curl https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug>/destinations/<destination id>/secret \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..."
# {"secret": "whsec_..."}

# Dry run: the exact request it would send for the newest capture, nothing is sent
curl -X POST https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug>/destinations/preview \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"destinationId": "<destination id>"}'

# Send the newest capture (or a sample) once and see what your server answered
curl -X POST https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug>/destinations/<destination id>/test \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..."
# {"status": 200, "durationMs": 182, "excerpt": "ok", "error": null, "delivered": true, "sample": false, "kind": "email", "format": "json", "filterPasses": true, ...}
```

A destination's fields (all optional except `url` when adding one; `PATCH` changes only what is sent):

| Field | Values |
|-------|--------|
| `url` | `https` on a public host name, at most 2048 characters |
| `name` | A label, at most 100 characters |
| `enabled` | Default `true` |
| `http`, `email` | Which kinds it receives; both default `true`, at least one must be on |
| `format` | `auto` (default: chat for Slack and Discord webhook URLs, otherwise HTTP as received and emails as signed JSON), `as_received`, `json`, `template`, `chat`, `postmark`, `sendgrid`, `mailgun`, `cloudmailin`, `sheets`, `file_drop` |
| `filter` | `{ "logic": "and" \| "or", "conditions": [...] }` or `null`: only captures that match are sent (the rule language of response rules, plus `kind`, `email`, `email_field`, `spam_score`, `email_auth` and `signature` fields); the rest are settled as `skipped` |
| `bodyTemplate` | For `template`: any JSON value with `{{ path \| filter }}` placeholders in its strings, such as `{"order": "{{ parsed.fields.order }}", "type": "{{ json.type }}"}` |
| `messageTemplate` | For `chat`: the message text with placeholders |
| `headers` | Up to 10 of `{ "name", "value" }`; values come back masked, a `null` value keeps the stored one |
| `appendPath` | Add the path after the slug to the URL for relayed requests; default `true` |
| `retrySeconds` | `86400` (default), `3600`, or `0` for a single try |
| `keepOrder` | One delivery at a time, in capture order |
| `sentField` | A JSON body field holding the sender's own timestamp |
| `throttleSeconds`, `delaySeconds` | 0 to 3600: at most one delivery every N seconds; wait N seconds before the first try |
| `attachments` | How an email's files travel in JSON: `links` (signed download links), `inline` (base64) or `none` |
| `config`, `dropSecret` | Settings of `sheets` and `file_drop` destinations (see File Drops below) |

Formats: `as_received` relays an HTTP request with its own method, headers, query string and exact bytes, plus `webhooks-cc-*` metadata headers signed with the destination's secret (`webhooks-cc-signature`). `json` sends signed JSON (below) for an email, and a JSON description of an HTTP request. `template` sends your own JSON body, signed like `json`. `chat` posts a message to a Slack or Discord webhook. `postmark`, `sendgrid`, `mailgun` and `cloudmailin` send an email the way that inbound mail service posts it, so a handler written for one of them works unchanged. `sheets` appends rows to a Google Sheet (connect the Google account and pick the spreadsheet in the dashboard). A destination whose URL answers `410 Gone` is switched off.

### The legacy single-URL API

Code written before destinations keeps working. The endpoint fields `forwardUrl`, `forwardEnabled`, `forwardHttp`, `forwardEmail`, `forwardFormat`, `forwardHeaders`, `forwardAppendPath`, `forwardRetrySeconds`, `forwardKeepOrder` and `forwardSentField` (set with `PATCH /api/endpoints/<slug>`) read and write the endpoint's primary destination, the one whose `role` is `forward`; `GET` and `POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/forwarding` read and rotate its secret, and `POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/forwarding/test` tests it. `notificationUrl` stands for a chat destination named Notifications (`role: "notify"`, at most one message a second, not retried). Prefer the destination routes in new code: they reach every destination, not only the first.

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"forwardUrl": "https://example.com/hooks/email", "forwardEnabled": true}'
```

`forwardEnabled: true` needs a `forwardUrl`. Endpoint objects carry `forwardEnabled`, `hasForwardSecret`, `destinationCount` and (for the owner only) `forwardUrl`.

### The request

```http
POST /hooks/email HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: webhooks.cc (+https://webhooks.cc/docs/forwarding)
webhook-id: msg_0b9e5f3a6c1d4f7e9a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b
webhook-timestamp: 1791450602
webhook-signature: v1,K5oZfzN95Z9UVu1EsfQmfVNQhnkZ2pj9o9NDN/H/pI4=
```

The body is the same JSON the dashboard's JSON tab shows for the email:

```typescript
interface ForwardedEmail {
  type: "email.received";
  timestamp: string;               // ISO 8601, when the email arrived; the same on every copy
  data: {
    id: string;                    // the request id; webhook-id is "msg_" + this id without dashes
    endpoint: { slug: string; name: string | null };
    receivedAt: string;            // ISO 8601
    address: string;               // the address it arrived at, tag included
    tag: string | null;
    subject: string | null;
    from: EmailAddress | null;     // the first From address
    to: EmailAddress[];
    cc: EmailAddress[];
    replyTo: EmailAddress[];
    date: string | null;
    messageId: string | null;
    inReplyTo: string[];
    text: string | null;           // up to 256 KB; derived from the HTML when there is no text part
    html: string | null;           // up to 256 KB
    codes?: string[];              // one-time codes; left out when showEmailExtracts is false
    links?: { url: string; text: string | null }[];  // links worth clicking; same rule
    attachments: {                 // with url or base64 content, per the destination
      filename: string | null;
      contentType: string;
      size: number;
      contentId: string | null;
      inline: boolean;
    }[];
    auth: { spf: string | null; dkim: string | null; dmarc: string | null; tls: string | null };
    headers: Record<string, string>;  // lowercase names, repeated headers joined with "\n"
    size: number;                  // whole message in bytes
    truncated: { text: boolean; html: boolean };
    test: boolean;                 // the "Send test email" sample, or the sample a test delivery sends
  };
}
```

### Verify the signature (Standard Webhooks)

The signature is `v1,` followed by the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `${webhook-id}.${webhook-timestamp}.${rawBody}`. The key is the base64 after the `whsec_` prefix of the secret, decoded. `webhook-signature` may hold several space-separated signatures; accept the request when any matches. Verify against the raw body before parsing JSON, compare in constant time, and reject a `webhook-timestamp` more than 300 seconds from your clock.

With the SDK, `verifyForwardedEmail` checks the headers, the timestamp (300 seconds by default) and the signature, and returns the typed event. It takes a Fetch `Headers`, a plain object or name and value pairs, and the raw body as a string, `Uint8Array` or `ArrayBuffer`:

```typescript
import { verifyForwardedEmail, WebhookVerificationError } from "@webhooks-cc/sdk";

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  try {
    const event = await verifyForwardedEmail(await request.text(), request.headers, process.env.FORWARD_SECRET!);
    // event.type === "email.received"; event.data is typed
    return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof WebhookVerificationError) {
      return new Response(error.message, { status: error.code === "invalid_payload" ? 400 : 401 });
    }
    throw error;
  }
}
```

(`verifyStandardWebhookSignature(body, headers, secret)` also accepts a Fetch `Headers` now, but checks the signature only, not the timestamp.)

In Node without dependencies:

```typescript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

function verify(rawBody: string, headers: Record<string, string>, secret: string): boolean {
  const id = headers["webhook-id"];
  const timestamp = headers["webhook-timestamp"];
  if (!id || !timestamp || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(timestamp)) > 300) return false;
  const key = Buffer.from(secret.replace(/^whsec_/, ""), "base64");
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", key).update(`${id}.${timestamp}.${rawBody}`).digest();
  return (headers["webhook-signature"] ?? "").split(" ").some((part) => {
    const given = Buffer.from(part.replace(/^v1,/, ""), "base64");
    return given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(given, expected);
  });
}
```

The official Standard Webhooks libraries (https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks) verify these headers too. Rotating the secret (`POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/forwarding`) signs every delivery from then on with the new one, retries included.

### Delivery and retries

- Any `2xx` answer accepts a delivery. Redirects are not followed and count as failures. Your server has 15 seconds to answer.
- A failed delivery is retried after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 3 hours, 6 hours and 12 hours (about a day in all), then marked failed.
- Every copy of one email has the same `webhook-id`, so a handler can skip repeats. Delivery is at least once, in no guaranteed order.
- A retry goes to the URL and secret saved at that moment. Switching a destination off, removing it, or taking a kind away from it marks its deliveries still waiting as failed.
- `retrySeconds` shortens the schedule: `3600` stops after an hour, `0` makes one try.
- `POST /api/requests/<id>/deliveries` queues a redelivery with the current settings, to every destination that takes the request or to `{ "destinationId": "..." }`; `POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/deliveries/redeliver-failed` does it for everything that failed.
- `POST /api/requests/<id>/replay` and `POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/replay` (`since`, `until` in ms, at most 500) read emails again with the current layouts and fields before sending them, for use after fixing a pattern.

Delivery history (`GET /api/requests/<id>/deliveries`, newest first, up to 20):

```typescript
interface Delivery {
  id: string;
  requestId: string;
  kind: "http" | "email";
  status: "pending" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "skipped"; // skipped: the filter turned it down
  destination: { id: string; name: string | null; url: string } | null; // null once it is removed
  format: string | null;           // how it went out: "json", "as_received", "chat", ...
  target: string | null;           // host and path it went to (host only for Slack and Discord)
  senderAt: number | null;         // the sender's own timestamp, when the request had one
  senderSource: string | null;
  attempts: number;
  createdAt: number;               // Unix ms
  finishedAt: number | null;
  nextAttemptAt: number | null;    // set while pending
  lastStatus: number | null;
  lastError: string | null;
  attemptLog: {                    // newest first
    attemptedAt: number;
    status: number | null;         // null when no answer arrived
    durationMs: number;
    error: string | null;
    responseExcerpt: string | null; // start of the response body, up to 1 KB
  }[];
}
```

`GET /api/endpoints/<slug>/deliveries` returns the endpoint's delivery log without the attempts (`limit` 1 to 100, default 5; `status=all|pending|failed|skipped`; `destination=<id>`; `before=<cursor>` for older rows): `id`, `requestId`, `kind`, `status`, `destination`, `attempts`, `createdAt`, `finishedAt`, `nextAttemptAt`, `lastStatus`, `lastError`, `lastDurationMs`, `format`, `senderAt`, `senderSource`, `cursor`, and the request's `method`, `path`, `receivedAt` and (for an email) `subject`. `GET /api/endpoints/<slug>/deliveries/summary` returns the counts.

### Alerts

`GET` and `PUT /api/endpoints/<slug>/alerts` (owner only, every plan) read and change when the endpoint tells its owner that something stopped working: `enabled`, `fieldFailures` (emails in a row that miss a required field, 1 to 100 or `null`), `fieldFailureShare` (percent of the last 20 emails, or `null`), `requiredFields` (names, or `null` for all), `silenceHours` (hours without an email, 1 to 720 or `null`), `destinationFailures` (a delivery failed after every retry), `notifyEmail`, and `notifyDestinationIds` (destinations that also get a chat message or a signed `alert.opened` / `alert.resolved` JSON event). `GET` also returns the latest `events`: `{ "id", "kind": "fields" | "silence" | "destination", "subject", "openedAt", "resolvedAt", "details" }`. Alerts carry field names and delivery errors, never an email's contents.

### Limits

- An endpoint has at most 10 destinations, and at most 1,000 deliveries wait for one destination at a time.
- The URL must be `https` on a public host name, at most 2048 characters: no IP addresses, `localhost`, private networks, credentials in the URL, or mail, database and other internal ports. A URL on webhooks.cc's own capture host is refused.
- On webhooks.cc, requests come from Cloudflare's network, not a fixed address. Do not allowlist IPs; check the signature.
- An email whose JSON would be larger than 10 MB is not forwarded.
- Deliveries are kept as long as the email itself.

## Layouts and Attachment Parsing

Docs: https://webhooks.cc/docs/layouts

A layout says how an endpoint reads one sender's or one kind of email: which emails it is for, which values to pick out, which rows to turn into line items, and whether to parse the attachments. Layouts are tried in order and the first whose conditions hold applies. The result travels with the email as `parsed`: in the API (`GET /api/requests/<id>`), in every forwarded delivery, in templates (`{{ parsed.fields.order }}`, `{{ item.sku }}`), in the SDKs and in the MCP tools. Emails on an endpoint with layouts are delivered once they are parsed, usually within seconds.
