Layouts are part of the endpoint: send the whole list with `PATCH /api/endpoints/<slug>` (owner only; `null` or `[]` removes them).

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"layouts": [{
    "id": "acme",
    "name": "Acme orders",
    "match": {"conditions": [{"field": "email", "name": "subject", "op": "contains", "value": "Order"}]},
    "fields": [{"name": "order", "from": "subject", "pattern": "#(\\d+)"}],
    "lineItems": {"from": "text", "pattern": "(?P<sku>[A-Z]+-\\d+)\\s+x(?P<qty>\\d+)\\s+(?P<price>[\\d.]+)"},
    "parseAttachments": true
  }]}'
```

- `match`: conditions in the rule language of destination filters (`{ "logic"?, "conditions": [...] }`); none takes every email.
- `fields`: up to 20 of `{ "name", "from": "subject" | "text" | "html" | "from" | "to" | "header", "header"?, "pattern" }`. Patterns are RE2; the first group is the value.
- `lineItems`: `{ "from": "text" | "html", "pattern", "start"?, "end"? }`, an RE2 pattern with named groups found again and again, optionally between two markers; or `"from": "attachment"` with `attachment` (a file name pattern) and `sheet`, whose rows become the line items. At most 1,000 line items per email.
- `parseAttachments`: CSV and TSV (rows), XLSX, XLS and ODS (rows per sheet), PDF (the text layer per page, no OCR), TXT, JSON, XML and ICS (text). Files over 32 MB, encrypted files and malformed files are reported with an `error` instead.

The exact layout schema is `Layout` in https://webhooks.cc/openapi.yaml.

`parsed` on an email:

```json
{
  "status": "matched",
  "layout": { "id": "acme", "name": "Acme orders" },
  "fields": { "order": "1001" },
  "lineItems": [{ "sku": "A-1", "qty": "2", "price": "9.50" }],
  "lineItemColumns": ["sku", "qty", "price"],
  "attachments": [{ "index": 0, "filename": "order-1001.csv", "format": "csv", "pages": 1, "sheets": [] }],
  "pages": 1
}
```

`status` is `no_layout` when no layout matched; the email is still captured and delivered. `parsed` is `null` while the parse is pending.

- Try before saving: `POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/layouts/preview` with `{ "layouts"?, "requestId"? }` returns `{ "problems", "layoutsCap", "request", "parsed" }` for a captured email. It saves nothing and uses no pages.
- Ready-made layouts: `POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/layouts/template` with `{ "template": "<id>" }` adds one of `shopify-orders`, `woocommerce-orders`, `etsy-sales`, `amazon-seller-orders`, `ebay-sales`, `stripe-receipts`, `paypal-payments`, `booking-com-reservations`, `airbnb-reservations`, `calendly-bookings`, `form-responses`, `csv-reports`, `pdf-invoices` (examples at https://mailhooks.cc/parse).
- After changing a layout, replay earlier emails to read them again: `POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/replay`.
- AI setup (propose patterns from up to 5 of the endpoint's own emails) is a dashboard feature that needs a signed-in person's consent on each ask; it is not offered to API keys. The patterns it writes are ordinary layouts.
- Parsed pages: each started 1,000 rows of a sheet or CSV, each PDF page and each text file is a page; a file uses at most 100. Free includes 20 pages a month, Pro 100, Business 2,000 (then page blocks or overage). Fields and line items read from the email's text never count. Without pages left, emails are still delivered, with attachments unparsed (`error: "limit"`).
- Layouts used per endpoint: 2 on Free, Pro and Teams, up to 50 on Business and Team Business. Layouts past the plan's number are kept but not matched (`layoutsCap` on the endpoint).

---

## Custom Inbound Domains

Docs: https://webhooks.cc/docs/email-capture#your-own-domain

On Business (and for a Team Business team) mail can also arrive at a domain the account owns, such as `orders@inbound.acme.example`, instead of `<slug>@mailhooks.cc`.

1. Add the domain under Account > Domains in the dashboard (a team's on the team's page).
2. Add two DNS records: a TXT record `_mailhooks.<domain>` with the value `mailhooks-verify=<token from the page>`, and an MX record for `<domain>` pointing at `mx.mailhooks.cc`. Use a subdomain that receives no other mail, because the MX record sends all of its mail here.
3. Check the records on the page. Once verified, mail is accepted within a minute.
4. Route it: an address per endpoint (`orders@` to one endpoint, `invoices@` to another) and, optionally, one endpoint for every other address. Plus tags work as on mailhooks.cc (`orders+test@` lands where `orders@` does).

- Mail to a custom domain is an ordinary captured email: the same request list, API, layouts and destinations, with the recipient address as `path`.
- The records are checked every day; after three failed checks in a row the domain lapses and its mail is refused until the records are back.
- Business includes one domain and Team Business one per team; each extra domain is $3 a month.
- An address at a verified domain cannot be used to sign up for an account, because its mail is readable here.
- Domains are managed in the dashboard only: the `/api/domains` routes take a signed-in session and answer `403` to an API key, and there are no SDK or MCP tools for them.

---

## File Drops

Docs: https://webhooks.cc/docs/forwarding#file-drops

A file drop is a destination that writes what the endpoint captures as CSV, XML or JSON files to the owner's own SFTP, FTPS, FTP or S3-compatible server, for systems that watch a folder (an ERP import, a warehouse system, a nightly job). Business, and Team Business for endpoints shared with the team.

```bash
curl -X POST https://webhooks.cc/api/endpoints/<slug>/destinations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer whcc_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "format": "file_drop", "name": "Orders to ERP", "http": false, "email": true,
    "config": {
      "protocol": "sftp", "host": "sftp.acme.example", "username": "orders", "folder": "incoming",
      "file": "csv", "rows": "line_items",
      "columns": [{"header": "Order", "value": "{{ parsed.fields.order }}"}, {"header": "SKU", "value": "{{ item.sku }}"}]
    },
    "dropSecret": {"password": "..."}
  }'
```

- `config.protocol`: `sftp` (`host`, `port` 22, `username`), `ftps` or `ftp` (`host`, `port` 21, `username`), or `s3` (`endpoint` URL, `region`, `bucket`, `accessKeyId`). `folder` is the folder (it must exist) or the S3 key prefix.
- `config.file`: `csv` (default) or `xml` with `columns` (up to 50 of `{ "header", "value" }`, values written with placeholders), or `json` (each email as the signed JSON format sends it). `rows`: `email` (a row per email) or `line_items` (a row per line item of a layout).
- `config.batch: true` writes one file for everything that arrives within the destination's `delaySeconds` (up to 3600) of a batch's first email, instead of a file per email. `config.prefix` goes before each file name.
- `dropSecret`: `{ "password" }`, `{ "privateKey" }` (SFTP, OpenSSH or PEM) or `{ "secretAccessKey" }` (S3). Write only and stored encrypted; the destination reports `hasDropSecret`. Changing the server, login, bucket, pinned host key or certificate fingerprint needs it sent again.
- SFTP host keys are pinned on the first connection (`config.hostKey`); a different key afterwards stops the drop. `config.tlsFingerprint` accepts one self-signed certificate (FTPS, S3).
- `POST /api/endpoints/<slug>/destinations/<id>/test` logs in and writes `webhooks-cc-test.txt` to the folder.
- Files are named after the time and the first request's id (`orders-20261029-173326-3f2a9c1e.csv`), written under a temporary name and renamed, so a watcher never sees half a file; a retry replaces its own file.
- Connections come from `mx.mailhooks.cc`; allow that address if the server only takes known ones. A refused login or a missing folder fails at once; an unreachable server is retried like any delivery.
- The MCP server does not offer file drops, so an agent never handles a server password; use the REST API, an SDK or the dashboard.

---

## Rate Limits

- Endpoint creation: 30 per 10 minutes
- Send test: 30 per minute
- Send test email: 10 per minute
- Forwarding and destination test delivery: 10 per minute
- Adding and changing destinations: 60 per minute per account
- Destination and response previews: 120 per minute
- Layouts preview: 20 per minute; email fields preview: 30 per minute
- Redeliver a request: 30 per minute; redeliver all failed: 10 per minute
- Replay one request: 60 per minute; replay a time range: 10 per minute
- Search: 60 per 10 minutes
- Search count: 120 per 10 minutes
- Guest endpoint creation: 20 per 10 minutes per IP
- Device auth: 10 per minute per IP

## Data Retention

- **Free plan**: 7 days
- **Pro plan**: 31 days
- **Business plan**: 90 days
- **Team-billed requests** (endpoints shared with an active team): 31 days, or 90 days on Team Business, whatever the owner's plan
- After moving to a plan with shorter retention, the old retention is kept for 7 more days
- Ephemeral endpoints: 12 hours, max 25 requests
- Emails and their forwarding deliveries follow the same retention as HTTP requests
- An endpoint can keep its requests for fewer days than the plan, or delete each one as soon as every destination has its copy
